items.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I played a concert with Wilbur Ware and Sonny Rollins in Philadelphia

ctx.x: Keiko mentioned you were influential in bringing Jimmy Garrison. Could you talk about that please?

Well Coltrane knew Jimmy Garrison from Philadelphia. They all knew each other. So when I mentioned his name—I played a concert with Wilbur Ware and Sonny Rollins in Philadelphia so before Sonny was giving all his interviews with all these bass players I said, “What the heck what’s a matter with him?” and he’s having all these auditions and I said “Man, you’ve got to be nuts.” There was one guy who played with the Philadelphia Symphony Orchestra and I thought he was pretty good. Then Jimmy Garrison came in and we…

So now the classic quartet is formed and ‘60, ‘61, ‘62 a very prolific period, a lot of recordings, Impulse. And then ’61 you do your first date as a leader for Riverside. Do you want to talk about that date and how that came about?

items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: Elvin say, "Sure." Well, this was a gig for me, you know?

ctx.x: And Wilbur Campbell went back to Chicago, and Frankie Dunlap made one side of the record, too, because Wilbur had to leave the next month after the initial side, and Junior Mance had left, and so we used Kenny Drew down at Birdland, but it was a beautiful night, and amost every other night, I had ... Monday night I had a job down there.

And he called me up for a gig -- Mr. Stan Getz, and Elvin Jones, Wynton Elmer, Joe Kelly and myself, and we were working -- that's Red Garland, Philly Joe, Trane, Paul, and himself opposite the Miles Davis Quintet -- at Birdland.

Naturally, we were gonna cook -- we were gonna play our best, too, and not realizing, you know, Stan Getz -- he's a star; naturally he's a star, but we want to get behind and push him just as much; the rhythm section was pushing Miles. And I don't know, Stan was going through his little problems during that time, and the other one was playing all those poly-rhythms, and Stan was getting confused; he didn't know what to do, so after the first set, we come off the bandstand, and he says, "Elvin" and Elton turned…
